newsitem.title: USA: Reynolds sees growing aluminum market.
newsitem.headline: Reynolds sees growing aluminum market.

text.p: Reynolds Metals Co chairman Jeremiah Sheehan said Wedensday that the company expects to see U.S. aluminum shipments increase four percent to five percent in 1997, and that global consumption should rise bewteen five percent and six percent.

Speaking at the company's annual shareholders meeting, he also said that Reynolds anticipates strong growth in aluminumn consumption, in excess of the growth rate of the gross domestic product, through 1999.
Reynolds has also, said Sheehan, formed a new unit that will concentrate on emerging markets such as China, Russia and India.
Sheehan said that as a result of the company's ongoing reorganization, it expects to see an unspecified number of jobs lost, especially at its corporate headquarters.

Reynolds, he said, is proceeding with asset sales as well. It has already announced plans for its real estate and coal operations, and has signed contracts for the sale of one extrusion plant to Tredegar Industries Inc and one to Kaiser Aluminum Corp. Other asset sales, said Sheehan, could not be publicly idenitifed yet.
Sheehan also said that the company is reviewing a possible spin-off of its packaging business, but did not specify if or when such a spin-off might occur.
